Hi Elena — thanks again for taking time earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

Summary from call:
- Primary use case: Aurora will send PHI-containing clinical notes (lab results, encounter summaries) to Redwood for enrichment and summarization via an LLM pipeline.
- Volume estimate: initial pilot ~50k messages / month, ramp to ~500k over 6 months.
- Priority questions: BAA availability, which deployment modes are eligible for PHI, SOC 2 status, encryption/KMS, and vendor security questionnaire.

What Redwood can confirm now:
- BAA: Redwood is willing to sign a BAA. We typically execute BAAs for Dedicated and Private deployments (see note below about hosted).
- Eligible deployment modes for PHI: Dedicated (reserved GPU capacity) and Private (VPC / on-prem) are supported for PHI processing. Our hosted multi-tenant public API is generally not used for PHI unless a specific architectural isolation and contractual exception is agreed — we can discuss if you want us to evaluate hosted for limited use, but the cleaner path is Dedicated or Private.
- SOC 2: Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II. I will share a redacted report on the next email.
- Encryption & KMS: Encryption in transit (TLS 1.2+) and at rest; customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) supported for Private and Dedicated.

Proposed next steps:
1) Please confirm the PHI types and retention windows you expect (short bullet list).
2) I will share: (a) HIPAA overview doc, (b) redacted SOC 2 report, (c) draft BAA for initial review.
3) If you have a vendor security questionnaire (PDF/Doc), please send it and we’ll populate answers; otherwise we can provide our standard security questionnaire link.
4) I’ll loop in Vivek (Head of Security) for detailed technical Qs and legal for the BAA negotiation.

Attachments (sent in follow-up): redwood-hipaa-overview.pdf, SOC2-report-redacted.pdf

Thanks — available for a 30-min follow-up next week if helpful.

Hi Elena / team — taking the security lead on this thread. Thanks for the questionnaire — I’ve started populating answers and wanted to summarize the key points here so procurement/legal have quick visibility. I’ve attached a draft BAA with standard Redwood language and the partially completed Aurora vendor questionnaire in the shared drive link.

Top-level technical summary (short):
- SOC 2: Redwood is covered by SOC 2 Type II with the following in-scope services: Redwood inference runtime, control plane for model routing and orchestration, API gateway, and telemetry/logging services. Redacted report attached to Marissa's email; we can provide an auditor contact under NDA.
- PHI processing & Eligible Modes: PHI processing is supported only on Dedicated and Private deployments.
  - Dedicated: single-tenant GPU pools reserved for Aurora; data at rest encrypted with customer KMS (optional); network segmentation and VPC peering available.
  - Private: customer-managed VPC/on-prem options, full control over network and keys.
  - Hosted Multi-tenant: not approved for PHI by default. De-identified or pseudonymized data is fine on hosted, but any PHI must go to Dedicated/Private.
- Encryption & Keys: TLS for all in-transit data; AES-256 at rest. Customer-managed KMS/HSM supported in Dedicated and Private; in hosted we use provider-managed keys unless specifically contracted.
- Access controls & auditing: RBAC, MFA for console access, privileged access reviews, and immutable audit logs for admin/API actions. We can provide sample audit log snippets and explain retention windows.
- Data retention & deletion: configurable retention policies per customer; we support data deletion workflows and can provide a deletion certificate on request after deprovisioning.
- Monitoring & incident response: 24/7 Security Operations, defined incident response playbooks, and notification SLAs included in our enterprise contract.

Attachments provided to Aurora team via shared Drive: BAA-draft-Aurora.docx (initial), Redwood_VSQ_answers_Aurora.xlsx (partially completed), SOC2-report-redacted.pdf.

Next steps I propose:
1) Legal: review the BAA draft and flag any redlines; we can use DocuSign for execution.
2) Technical call: schedule a 30-min call (we have availability Mon/Tue next week) to go through the questionnaire items we left as "needs customer input" (retention windows, KMS choices, dataflow diagrams).
3) Pilot setup: once BAA signed, we can spin up a Dedicated pilot environment (estimated lead time: ~2 weeks from signed SOW + infra start).

If helpful, here are straightforward answers to some of the procurement items: 
- Data residency: US-only region options available for Dedicated/Private.
- Third-party subprocessors: list available on request (we have a standard subprocessors list; will provide link).
- Pen-testing & vulnerability scans: annual third-party penetration test results available; we provide summary reports under NDA.

Happy to hop on a call with your team — suggest Mon 10/5 10:00am PT or Tue 10/6 9:00am PT.

Regards,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Security, Redwood Inference
